title: Best Compliant AI Voice Agents for BFSI (2026)
summary: Compare 8 compliant AI voice agent platforms for banking, financial services, and insurance based on security, compliance, telephony, scalability, integrations, and pricing.
body_markdown:
The AI voice agent market is expected to reach[$3.5 billion in 2026 and grow to $35.2 billion by 2033, at a CAGR of 39%](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/ai-voice-agents-market-report) . BFSI was also the largest end-use segment in 2025, driven by use cases across banking, insurance, loans, customer support, and fraud alerts.


But using AI voice agents in BFSI comes with a different set of requirements. These platforms may handle financial information, customer identities, payment details, call recordings, and other sensitive data. So alongside voice quality and automation, teams need to think about compliance, data security, access controls, data residency, auditability, and how customer data moves through the underlying AI and telephony stack.


In this guide, we compare 8 AI voice agent platforms to see which are best suited for banking, financial services, and insurance teams, based on their compliance coverage, security, telephony infrastructure, integrations, scalability, and pricing.


## TL;DR


-


**Plivo:** Best overall for BFSI teams that want compliant AI voice agents, owned telephony, global reach, and predictable pricing in one stack.


-


**Vapi:** Best for developer-led BFSI teams that want full control over the LLM, voice, transcription, and telephony providers they use.


-


**Retell AI:** Best for teams that want to launch compliant voice workflows quickly without building the full stack themselves.


-


**Bland AI:** Best for high-volume inbound and outbound calling where enterprise compliance and scale matter.


-


**Synthflow AI:** Best for operations teams that want a no-code way to build compliant voice workflows with less engineering support.


-


**ElevenLabs:** Best when natural-sounding, multilingual conversations are the priority, while still supporting enterprise compliance requirements.


-


**Twilio:** Best for banks and insurers already running customer communications on Twilio infrastructure.


-


**LiveKit:** Best for engineering teams building highly customized, real-time voice or multimodal applications with deeper control over the underlying stack.


If you want one platform that brings AI voice agents, telephony, compliance, global connectivity, and straightforward per-minute pricing together, Plivo is the platform we would shortlist first for BFSI.


## Does the compliance certification cover the actual voice product?


A vendor saying it is “SOC 2 compliant” does not automatically mean every part of its AI voice setup is covered.


For BFSI teams, the important question is what the certification actually includes. Does it cover the AI voice agent itself? What about the telephony layer, call recordings, transcripts, analytics, and any third-party LLM or speech providers involved?


This matters because a voice agent can pass customer data through several different systems during a single call. If some of those systems sit outside the vendor’s compliance scope, your security team may still need to review them separately.


Before signing, ask the vendor for the scope of its SOC 2 or ISO certification, its subprocessor list, and a clear data-flow diagram showing where customer data is processed and stored.


That last line makes the section especially BOFU because it gives the reader something concrete to ask during procurement.


## How We Evaluated These AI Voice Agent Platforms


For this comparison, we looked beyond basic voice quality or how impressive the demo sounds. For BFSI teams, the bigger question is whether the platform can hold up under real compliance, security, and operational requirements.


Here are the main factors we used to evaluate each platform:


**1. Compliance Coverage:** We looked at certifications and frameworks such as SOC 2, PCI DSS, GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO standards, along with whether they are relevant to the actual voice product.


**2. Data Handling and Residency:** We considered where customer data is processed and stored, how recordings and transcripts are handled, and whether teams can control data residency and retention.


**3. Telephony Infrastructure:** We looked at whether the platform owns more of the telephony stack itself or depends on third-party providers. This matters for data flow, reliability, latency, and the number of vendors your security team may need to review.


**4. Access Controls and Auditability:** For BFSI use cases, features like SSO, RBAC, audit logs, admin controls, and activity tracking can matter just as much as the AI itself.


**5. Human Handoffs:** We looked at how easily the AI can transfer a customer to a human agent when the conversation involves fraud, disputes, financial hardship, complex claims, or other sensitive situations.


**6. Integrations:** The platform should be able to connect with the systems BFSI teams already use, including CRM, core banking or insurance systems, payment platforms, fraud tools, and internal APIs.


**7. Scalability and Reliability:** We considered concurrency, global coverage, latency, uptime, and how well the platform is likely to perform once call volumes move beyond a small pilot.


**8. Pricing:** Finally, we looked at the actual cost of running the platform, including whether telephony, transcription, LLM usage, and voice models are bundled or charged separately.


The goal was to evaluate each platform the way a BFSI security, operations, and procurement team would, not just based on which one sounds best in a demo.

For BFSI teams, the biggest difference is not simply which platform has the longest list of certifications. It is how much of the voice stack those controls actually cover. A platform may be compliant itself but still rely on separate telephony, speech, or model providers that your security team needs to review.


That is where **Plivo** stands out as a strong all-round option. It combines the AI agent and telephony layers with compliance controls, regional data residency, access controls, and auditability in a more integrated stack.


## 1. Plivo


Plivo is a strong fit for BFSI teams that want AI voice agents and telephony handled in the same stack. Instead of adding an AI layer on top of a separate phone provider, Plivo brings the voice agent and communications infrastructure together, which can make security reviews, data flows, and day-to-day operations easier to manage.


For banks, fintechs, lenders, and insurers, that setup is useful for workflows such as KYC follow-ups, fraud alerts, payment reminders, collections, policy renewals, claims follow-ups, and customer support.


### Key strengths


-


**Strong compliance coverage:** Plivo supports SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS, and CSA STAR requirements, giving BFSI teams coverage across a wide range of regulated workflows.


-


**Regional data residency:** Teams can keep data within supported US, EU, and APAC regions, which can matter when customer information cannot freely move across geographies.


-


**Owned telephony infrastructure:** Because Plivo handles both the AI agent and telephony layers, there are fewer third-party providers involved in each call.


-


**Access and security controls:** Enterprise teams get controls such as RBAC, audit logs, and encryption to help manage who can access sensitive customer data.


-


**Low-latency conversations:** Plivo reports sub-500 ms voice latency, which helps conversations feel more natural during verification, collections, or support calls.


-


**Global reach:** Support for 50+ languages and connectivity across 190+ countries makes it useful for BFSI companies operating across multiple markets.


-


**No-code + APIs:** Operations teams can build and adjust agents without relying on developers for every change, while engineering teams still get APIs for deeper integrations.


### Limitations


Plivo makes the most sense if you want a more integrated voice stack. If your engineering team specifically wants to choose separate telephony, speech, LLM, and orchestration providers, platforms like Vapi or LiveKit may give you more control over each individual layer.


Some enterprise capabilities, including broader compliance controls, higher concurrency, and more advanced deployment requirements, may also require an enterprise plan.


### Pricing


Plivo AI Voice Agents cost $0.04 per minute, with telephony, voice models, and transcription included in the rate. That makes the pricing easier to estimate compared with platforms where each layer of the voice stack is billed separately.


## 2. Vapi


Vapi is a good fit for BFSI teams that want more control over how their AI voice stack is put together. Instead of bundling telephony, transcription, voice, and LLMs into one setup, Vapi lets developers choose the providers they want for each layer.


That flexibility can be useful for banks, fintechs, and insurers with strong engineering teams and specific requirements around models, data handling, latency, or integrations.


### Key strengths


-


**Highly customizable:** Teams can choose their own LLM, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and telephony providers.


-


**Good for developer-led BFSI teams:** Vapi is API-first, which gives engineering teams more control over call logic, workflows, and backend integrations.


-


**Flexible deployment options:** Teams can configure different providers depending on their compliance, performance, and data-handling requirements.


-


**Enterprise security controls:** Vapi supports features such as SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA options, PCI support, SSO, RBAC, and audit logging.


-


**Useful for custom BFSI workflows:** It can be used for KYC calls, collections, fraud callbacks, claims follow-ups, and other voice workflows tied to existing banking or insurance systems.


### Limitations


The same flexibility that makes Vapi attractive can also make compliance reviews more complicated. If you use separate providers for telephony, transcription, voice, and LLMs, your security team may need to review each one rather than evaluating a single stack.


Pricing can also be harder to estimate because the platform fee is only one part of the final cost.


### Pricing


Vapi charges $0.05 per minute as a platform fee, with a realistic all-in cost of roughly $0.13 to $0.33 per minute depending on the telephony, transcription, LLM, and voice providers you choose.


## 3. Retell AI


Retell AI is a good fit for BFSI teams that want to get compliant voice workflows live quickly without building the entire stack from scratch. It brings agent building, telephony, testing, monitoring, call transfers, and post-call analysis into one platform.


That makes it useful for banks, lenders, fintechs, and insurers running workflows like KYC follow-ups, collections, fraud callbacks, claims support, and renewal reminders.


### Key strengths


-


**Faster deployment:** Retell gives teams most of the core voice-agent tooling in one place, which reduces the amount of setup needed before going live.


-


**Strong compliance coverage:** Retell supports SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and GDPR requirements, making it relevant for more regulated BFSI workflows.


-


**PII handling controls:** Features like PII redaction and configurable data retention can help teams manage sensitive customer information more carefully.


-


**SSO and RBAC:** Enterprise teams can control access more tightly across users and roles.


-


**Human transfers:** Calls can be escalated to a human agent when a conversation becomes sensitive or needs manual review.


-


**Post-call automation:** Retell can generate summaries, call outcomes, sentiment data, and custom fields that can be pushed into downstream systems.


### Limitations


Retell does not own the full telephony stack end to end, so some deployments may still depend on external carriers or telephony providers. For BFSI security teams, that can mean a few more components to review. Pricing can also vary quite a bit depending on the voice, model, telephony setup, and other features you use.


### Pricing


Retell AI costs $0.07 to $0.31 per minute, depending on the voice, model, telephony setup, and other components selected.


## 4. Bland AI


Bland AI is a strong option for BFSI teams that need to handle a high volume of inbound or outbound calls while still meeting enterprise security requirements. It is especially useful for workflows like collections, payment reminders, fraud verification, claims follow-ups, and other repetitive customer conversations.


Its setup is more enterprise and API-focused, so it tends to fit better with larger teams that already have engineering support and want more control over how voice workflows connect with existing systems.


### Key strengths


-


**Built for high call volumes:** Bland is designed for large-scale calling, which makes it useful for BFSI teams running collections, reminders, or verification campaigns.


-


**Strong compliance coverage:** Bland supports SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, GDPR, and PCI DSS requirements.


-


**Own AI infrastructure:** Bland runs its own voice and speech infrastructure, which can reduce reliance on external AI providers for customer call data.


-


**Flexible telephony setup:** Enterprise teams can connect their own SIP or telephony infrastructure instead of replacing their existing stack.


-


**Human handoffs:** Calls can be transferred to human agents when the conversation becomes sensitive or needs manual review.


-


**Useful for structured workflows:** Banks and insurers can build repeatable flows for verification, reminders, collections, and support.


### Limitations


Bland is more API and enterprise-focused than some of the easier no-code platforms. If your operations team wants to build and adjust agents without much developer involvement, the setup may feel heavier.


Telephony can also remain a separate layer depending on the configuration, which means your security and procurement teams may still need to review additional infrastructure.


### Pricing


Bland AI costs $0.14 per minute, with final costs depending on the plan, telephony setup, transfers, and enterprise requirements.


## 5. Synthflow AI


Synthflow AI is a good fit for BFSI teams that want to build compliant voice workflows without relying too heavily on developers. Its no-code approach makes it easier for operations teams to create and update flows for things like KYC follow-ups, collections, claims support, payment reminders, and policy renewals.


It is especially useful for teams that want to move quickly and keep day-to-day workflow changes out of the engineering queue.


### Key strengths


-


**No-code workflow builder:** Operations teams can create and adjust voice flows without writing much code.


-


**Good for repetitive BFSI workflows:** It works well for structured conversations such as reminders, follow-ups, verification steps, and routing.


-


**Compliance coverage:** Synthflow supports SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR requirements.


-


**Broad integrations:** Teams can connect CRMs, databases, ticketing tools, scheduling platforms, and external APIs.


-


**Human handoffs:** More complex or sensitive conversations can be routed to a human agent when needed.


-


**White-label support:** This can be useful for service providers or larger groups that want to deploy voice automation under their own brand.


### Limitations


Synthflow does not own the full telephony stack, so some deployments still depend on external carriers or SIP providers. For BFSI teams, that can mean additional vendors to review from a security and compliance perspective.


It also gives technical teams less control than more developer-focused platforms like Vapi or LiveKit, which may matter if you need a highly customized architecture.


### Pricing


Synthflow uses a pay-as-you-go pricing model, with final costs depending on call volume, telephony, AI models, and the features used.


## 6. ElevenLabs


ElevenLabs is a strong fit for BFSI teams that care a lot about voice quality and multilingual customer conversations. Its AI voices are among the more natural-sounding options, which can be useful for sensitive workflows like fraud alerts, payment reminders, claims follow-ups, or customer support.


It also gives teams a way to build voice agents without giving up enterprise security and compliance requirements.


### Key strengths


-


**Natural-sounding voice quality:** ElevenLabs is one of the stronger options if you want automated calls to feel less robotic.


-


**Multilingual support:** Useful for banks and insurers serving customers across multiple regions and languages.


-


**Compliance coverage:** ElevenLabs supports SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS, and several ISO certifications.


-


**Agent-building tools:** Teams get workflow tools, knowledge bases, multilingual agents, and configurable concurrency.


-


**Flexible telephony setup:** ElevenLabs can connect with existing telephony providers and SIP-based infrastructure.


-


**Good for customer-facing BFSI use cases:** It works well for reminders, verification calls, claims updates, and other conversations where customer experience matters.


### Limitations


ElevenLabs does not own the full telephony stack, so some deployments still depend on external providers. For BFSI teams, that means the security and compliance review may extend beyond ElevenLabs itself.


It is also more voice-focused than infrastructure-focused. If you want telephony, AI, compliance, and communications handled more tightly in one stack, a more integrated platform may be easier to manage.


### Pricing


ElevenLabs starts at $6 per month.


## 7. Twilio


Twilio is a strong fit for BFSI teams that already use its communications infrastructure and want to add AI voice agents on top. It gives teams the telephony, messaging, and orchestration layer while still letting them connect their own LLMs, business logic, and backend systems.


For larger banks, fintechs, and insurers with in-house engineering teams, that can work well for workflows like fraud alerts, payment reminders, collections, claims support, and customer service.


### Key strengths


-


**Owned telephony infrastructure:** Twilio operates the underlying voice network, phone numbers, routing, and SIP infrastructure, so teams do not need to add a separate telephony provider.


-


**Strong compliance coverage:** Twilio supports SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS, and multiple ISO certifications.


-


**Bring your own LLM:** Teams can connect the model they prefer rather than being locked into a single AI provider.


-


**Broader communications stack:** Voice can sit alongside SMS, WhatsApp, chat, and other Twilio products, which is useful for BFSI teams running multi-channel customer workflows.


-


**Enterprise security controls:** Larger teams can use features like SSO, access controls, and audit tooling to manage sensitive customer data more carefully.


-


**Good fit for existing Twilio users:** If your communication stack already runs on Twilio, adding AI voice is a natural extension rather than a complete rebuild.


### Limitations


Twilio takes more technical setup than some of the newer AI voice platforms. Teams still need to connect the LLM, build the agent logic, and manage integrations, so it is generally a better fit for companies with engineering resources.


Pricing can also be harder to estimate because telephony, AI usage, phone numbers, and other services may all be billed separately.


### Pricing


Twilio uses a pay-as-you-go pricing model, with final costs depending on the voice, telephony, AI, messaging, and other services used.


### 8. LiveKit


LiveKit is a good fit for BFSI teams with strong engineering resources that want more control over how their AI voice stack is built. It is designed for real-time voice, video, and multimodal applications, so it works well when the use case goes beyond a basic voice bot.


For banks, fintechs, and insurers, that flexibility can be useful for custom verification flows, customer support, fraud-response workflows, or more complex interactions tied closely to internal systems.


### Key strengths


-


**Built for real-time AI:** LiveKit is designed for low-latency voice and video interactions.


-


**Flexible AI stack:** Developers can choose their preferred speech-to-text, LLM, and text-to-speech providers.


-


**Native telephony support:** LiveKit supports inbound and outbound calling through SIP and can also provide phone numbers.


-


**Good for custom BFSI workflows:** Engineering teams can build their own verification, support, escalation, and backend logic around the agent.


-


**Compliance support:** LiveKit supports SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA requirements.


-


**Multimodal capabilities:** It is especially useful if your use case may eventually extend beyond voice into video or other real-time customer experiences.


### Limitations


LiveKit requires more engineering work than most platforms on this list. You are still building a large part of the application yourself, so it is not the best fit for BFSI teams that want something they can configure and launch with minimal development effort.


The modular setup can also make security and compliance reviews more involved, especially if you are using multiple external providers for telephony, speech, and AI models.


### Pricing


LiveKit starts at $50 per month, with additional usage costs depending on agent sessions, telephony, and the AI services used.


## Choosing the Right AI Voice Agent Platform for BFSI


The right platform depends on what matters most for your team. Some BFSI companies care more about compliance and data residency, while others need faster deployment, deeper customization, or a simpler way to manage telephony and AI in one place.


-


**If compliance and fewer moving parts are the priority:** Plivo is one of the strongest options if you want AI voice agents, telephony, compliance controls, global connectivity, and data residency handled more tightly in one stack. That can make procurement and security reviews simpler compared with setups where telephony, speech, and AI models come from several different providers.


-


**If you want to launch quickly:** Retell AI is a good fit for teams that want to get compliant voice workflows live without building everything from scratch. It gives you agent building, calling, monitoring, and post-call tooling in one place.


-


**If your operations team wants a no-code setup:** Synthflow AI works well when non-technical teams need to build and update voice workflows themselves. Plivo also offers a no-code builder while keeping APIs available for more complex integrations.


-


**If your engineering team wants full control:** Vapi gives developers more freedom to choose their own LLM, voice, transcription, and telephony providers. LiveKit is a better fit if you are building highly customized real-time voice or multimodal applications. The trade-off is that more flexibility usually means more vendors and a more involved compliance review.


-


**If voice quality is the main priority:** ElevenLabs is worth considering if natural-sounding and multilingual conversations matter most, especially for customer-facing workflows like reminders, support, and verification.


-


**If you're running very high call volumes:** Bland AI is a strong option for large-scale inbound and outbound workflows such as collections, payment reminders, and customer verification.


-


**If you already use Twilio:** Twilio is the natural place to start if your communications infrastructure is already built around it. If you are starting fresh, though, it is worth comparing the overall setup against a more integrated option like Plivo.


For BFSI teams, the best choice is rarely just the platform with the most certifications. What matters is how compliance, telephony, data handling, security controls, and AI all work together in practice. If you want that balance in one stack, Plivo is the platform we would shortlist first.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What makes an AI voice agent compliant for BFSI?


A compliant AI voice agent should do more than hold a certification. BFSI teams should look at how customer data is processed, where recordings and transcripts are stored, whether access is controlled, and which third-party providers are involved in the voice stack. Certifications like SOC 2, PCI DSS, GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO standards can all matter depending on the use case.


### Which AI voice agent platform is best for BFSI?


There is no single best platform for every team. Plivo is a strong all-round option if you want AI voice agents, owned telephony, compliance controls, global coverage, and more predictable pricing in one stack. Vapi and LiveKit are better suited to developer-led teams, while Retell AI and Synthflow are easier to get up and running quickly.


### Is SOC 2 enough for an AI voice agent used in banking?


Not necessarily. SOC 2 is important, but banking teams may also need to consider PCI DSS, GDPR, data residency, encryption, access controls, audit logs, and the compliance posture of any telephony, LLM, transcription, or voice providers involved in the workflow.


### Can AI voice agents be used for sensitive BFSI workflows?


Yes, depending on the platform and how it is configured. AI voice agents can support use cases such as KYC follow-ups, fraud alerts, collections, payment reminders, claims support, and policy renewals. Sensitive or high-risk conversations should still have clear rules for human escalation.


### What should BFSI teams check before buying an AI voice agent platform?


Look beyond voice quality. Check the platform's compliance scope, data residency options, retention controls, access management, auditability, telephony setup, integrations, human handoffs, reliability, and total cost at scale. For BFSI teams, the way the full voice stack handles customer data is usually more important than how impressive the demo sounds.
